name: Tessera Industries Optical Disruptor OD-4 'Strobe'
description: A handheld directed energy device that emits a rapidly cycling pattern of high-intensity light at frequencies calculated to induce seizure-like neural disruption in human visual processing. The OD-4 projects a beam of strobing light that cycles through specific frequencies known to cause photosensitive responses — disorientation, nausea, loss of motor control, and in approximately 3% of targets, full tonic-clonic seizures. The beam is effective against both augmented and unaugmented targets because it exploits fundamental biological visual processing rather than electronic systems.
specifications:
beam type: High-intensity cycling visible light
frequency: Calculated photosensitive disruption pattern
effective range: 5-50 meters directional
effect: Disorientation, nausea, motor loss, 3% seizure risk
power: Rechargeable capacitor, 30 seconds continuous
weight: 0.4 kg
form factor: Pistol-sized handheld
countermeasure: Light-filtering eyewear or closed eyes
story_hooks: An OD-4 was used in a crowded venue and triggered seizures in eleven people — the operator did not know or care about the 3% seizure risk in a crowd of 400.
A modified OD-4 has been tuned to a frequency that specifically disrupts the visual processing of Axiom-model neural interfaces, causing permanent damage to the optical enhancement firmware.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular pistol-grip device with a pronounced forward-projecting lens assembly. The OD-4 has an aggressive wedge shape that tapers toward its emitter, suggesting focused intensity. Its compact profile belies its specialized function — it reads as a precision instrument rather than a conventional firearm.
physical_description.dimensions: 21 cm length, 8 cm grip width, 6 cm height. Lens assembly projects 4 cm forward from body.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light and balanced — 0.4 kg feels almost insubstantial in the palm, allowing for quick directional tracking without arm fatigue. Weight distribution centers toward the grip.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy frame with polycarbonate lens housing. Thermal dissipation channels integrated into barrel shroud.
physical_description.finish: Satin titanium with matte black polymer grip sections. The lens housing has a faint iridescent coating that shifts from deep purple to cyan under direct light, hinting at optical manipulation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray and matte black primary, with accent striping in electric blue around the lens bezel. Subtle Lumina Home Automation branding in silver.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized, slightly granular polymer with ergonomic finger grooves. Heat-dissipation design creates subtle ridged patterns that aid grip purchase even with gloved hands.
distinctive_features: Oversized lens assembly with internal multi-axis refracting optics visible through transparent sections
Three small LED status indicators (power, frequency lock, heat level) arranged vertically on right side
Cooling vents as radial lines across barrel shroud
Recessed power actuator with tactile feedback detent
Frequency calibration dial on left grip — marked with cryptic symbols instead of numbers
Faint residual heat shimmer visible around lens in thermal imaging
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Lumina Home Automation logomark stamped on left grip. 'TESSERA INDUSTRIES OD-4 STROBE' in small sans-serif text along barrel shroud. Serial number etched below grip. 'LICENSED RIOT CONTROL' warning label on barrel in yellow/black.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained and calibrated. Lenses kept pristine to preserve beam coherency. Frequent users show micro-scratches on grip from constant recalibration adjustments. Occasional dust deposits in cooling vents from field use in urban environments.
